A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same size-generalization research, with identifiable retained clustering methods, results and proofs despite the changed title and expanded scope. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original clustering-accuracy experiments, SoftmaxCenters comparisons and single-linkage sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 reports original clustering and max-cut experiments, including accuracy curves, rounding-sensitivity studies, runtime measurements and adaptive-selection results in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: v3 extends performance estimation with an induced-subgraph SDP proxy for GW and adds an adaptive selection procedure that increases subset sizes until performance or rankings stabilize (Appendix C.3). These add estimation and stopping components beyond v1's prescribed-budget clustering procedures; the clustering MCMC approach is retained.

E1.justification: The four clustering data sources are retained. v3 adds max-cut evaluation on Erdős–Rényi, barbell, random-geometric and Barabási–Albert graphs, an Internet AS panel in Figure 6, and a Petersen-graph deletion case study, substantially expanding task and graph coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated comparisons between GW, Greedy and their subsampled counterparts (Figure 1b and Appendix C), absent from v1. Within clustering, Gonzalez's heuristic disappears from the main accuracy comparison but remains in the appendix objective-value comparisons, so it is not removed altogether.

E3.justification: Main MNIST, GM and NC instance sizes change from 200 to 500, with additional 2000-point experiments and 4000-point, ten-cluster MNIST; Omniglot remains at 40 points. New max-cut protocols evaluate cut density on 50-node graphs, runtime on 500-node graphs, and adaptive sampling of 2–64 nodes from 100-node graphs.

E4.justification: v3 adds GW sensitivity to deleting one Petersen-graph node, comparisons of rounding distributions from different optimal SDP solutions, and adaptive ranking-stability analysis (Figures 4–5 and Table 2). Existing SoftmaxCenters parameter/size studies and single-linkage noise analyses are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: The main clustering experiments report 1000 trials in v3 versus 10000 repetitions in v1. Main-figure bands are described as two standard errors instead of 95% confidence intervals, without establishing a different interval-construction procedure. New max-cut and adaptive experiments disclose 150 and 10 trials, respectively.

E6.justification: v3 replaces the main clustering curves under revised settings and adds max-cut densities, rounding distributions, rankings and timings. For example, Table 1 reports GW runtime of 961.4030 seconds at full size versus 72.2823 seconds at a 60% subsample. These are newly reported results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices E.3–E.4 add SDP subsampling bounds, a GW rounding counterexample, GW performance bounds and a Greedy sample-complexity theorem with proofs. Retained clustering mathematics also changes: Definition 2.1 repairs the misclassification expression, and the stated single-linkage bound changes its cluster-size term from n/(min_i |C_i|)^2 to n/min_i |C_i|.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from semi-supervised clustering selection to accelerating data-driven selection for combinatorial partitioning across training instances. The abstract and conclusion now claim results for GW and Greedy alongside the three clustering algorithms; max-cut was future work in v1.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of why SDP-value convergence does not ensure equivalent GW rounding behavior and why its GW bounds include multiplicative error. Appendix C.3 also argues that empirical stabilization avoids unknown instance-dependent quantities. Its claim of stabilization in every case by 8–16 nodes is overstated: Table 2's random-geometric ranking reverses at 64 nodes and again on the full graph.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly states that experimental code is released and supplies a repository link; v1 has no corresponding access statement. v3 also documents generator parameters and sampling schedules for the added graph experiments, providing additional reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against property testing, max-cut/CSP approximation and SDP subsampling, including comparisons with Barak et al. and reliance on Mathieu and Schudy. It also adds sublinear clustering and sketch-and-solve literature while retaining the earlier distinction from clustering coresets.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around the broader algorithm-selection problem. The clustering sections are consolidated, substantial discussion moves to reorganized appendices, and an appendix contents page is added. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond inserting new scientific content.

P2.justification: v3 redesigns the main experiments into shared dataset panels overlaying clustering methods, changes horizontal axes to sampled fractions, and adds max-cut panels. New graph illustrations, rounding-distribution plots, and runtime and ranking tables substantially expand the displays; retained clustering illustrations and appendix plots are relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the clustering-error definition and adds broader validation, measured speedups and code-access information. However, its new Theorem 3.3 bounds randomized GW output without a rounding expectation; at full sampling this conflicts with Figure 5, which reports cuts of 5 from an SDP optimum of 9, below the asserted 0.878 factor. The adaptive-stability claim also conflicts with Table 2. These substantive inconsistencies affect the new guarantees and selection procedure, leaving the net quality change uncertain despite the useful additions.
